description: Head-to-head evaluation: does our agent beat rule_based_agent? Uses main.py's own designated comparison (--my-agent flag: 1 of our agents vs 3 built-in rule_based_agent instances), classic scenario, 50 rounds per run, across 5 independent fixed seeds per agent (250 rounds total per agent). Run 2026-09-14.
verdict: Yes, consistently. Both my_agent3 and my_agent_planning beat all three rule_based_agent opponents' scores in every one of the 5 seeds tested (5/5, no losses). Average total score is roughly 1.8x the best-performing rule_based_agent in the same match.
why_it_wins: Compared to the built-in rule_based_agent (3 instances per match), our agents consistently show a lower suicide rate (roughly 5-17 per 50 rounds vs rule_based_agent's own 19-30 per 50 rounds seen in the same matches), more kills, and more coins collected. The win is not from rule_based_agent's mistakes alone - our agent is both safer and more effective.
caveats: (1) Tested only in the classic scenario - the same agents' loot-crate-only performance (see hyperparam_sweep2_controlled_summary.json) shows a much higher self-destruction rate (~1.7-2.25 suicides/round) in that harder, bomb-dense scenario, so the classic-scenario win margin should not be assumed to hold in every scenario mix a grader might use. (2) 5 seeds is a solid sample for a course deadline but not exhaustive - an adversarial or unusual seed could still produce a bad round. (3) Both agents share my_agent3's underlying network and features, so this is not yet evidence that my_agent (PPO) or my_agent2 beat rule_based_agent - those were not part of this test.
